claims.claim: LURY-1 peptides showed similar efficacies and potencies for CHO-NPR-22b cells as for CHO-NPR-22a cells.
claims.source: When we used a stable CHO cell line expressing the B isoform of NPR-22 (CHO-NPR-22b), which is the only known splice variant of NPR-22a (Figure 2A), LURY-1 peptides showed similar efficacies and potencies to those for the CHO-NPR-22a cells (Figure 2F).
claims.evidence: Supported by calcium assay data shown in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: The lury-1 promoter drives expression of Venus specifically in M1 and M2 pharyngeal neurons.
claims.source: When the fluorescent reporter Venus was fused to the 3.5 kb lury-1 promoter (lury-1prom), the expression of Venus was observed only in two classes of pharyngeal neurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A). These neurons were identified as the M1 and M2 neurons (Figure 3A) by their morphology, position, and the co-expression of established cell markers (Kim and Li, 2004; Refai et al., 2013) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C).
claims.evidence: Supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-C, and citations to cell marker studies.

claims.claim: The lury-1prom::Venus reporter was robustly expressed in M1 in all larval stages and in adults.
claims.source: We found that the lury-1prom::Venus reporter was robustly expressed in M1 in all larval stages and in adults, whereas its expression in M2 was not detectable in most L1–L3 worms but started to increase from the L4 stage (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: Supported by developmental expression data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: Expression of lury-1prom::Venus in M2 was not detectable in most L1–L3 worms but started to increase from the L4 stage.
claims.source: We found that the lury-1prom::Venus reporter was robustly expressed in M1 in all larval stages and in adults, whereas its expression in M2 was not detectable in most L1–L3 worms but started to increase from the L4 stage (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: Supported by developmental expression data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: The lury-1prom::lury-1::Venus translational reporter produced fluorescent signals in coelomocytes as well as in M1 and M2 neurons.
claims.source: We also generated a lury-1prom::lury-1::Venus translational reporter, in which Venus is C-terminally fused in frame to the genomic lury-1-coding sequences containing introns. This translational reporter produced fluorescent signals in coelomocytes, which are macrophage-like scavenger cells that endocytose proteins secreted into the body cavity (Fares and Greenwald, 2001), as well as in the M1 and M2 neurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: Supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and citation to Fares and Greenwald, 2001.

claims.claim: The LURY-1 preproprotein is sorted into the secretory pathway and LURY-1 peptides can reach distant cells.
claims.source: This result implies that the LURY-1 preproprotein is sorted into the secretory pathway and that LURY-1 peptides can reach distant cells.
claims.evidence: Inferred from coelomocyte uptake of LURY-1::Venus translational reporter.

claims.claim: The npr-22 promoter drives Venus expression in many cells mainly in the head region including head muscles, I2 neurons, MC neurons, RIH neuron, AIA neurons, AUA neurons, ASK neurons, ASI neurons, B-type motorneurons, pharyngeal muscles, body wall muscles, intestine, and unidentified cells anterior to the nerve ring.
claims.source: The Venus reporter driven by the 5.7 kb npr-22 promoter was expressed in many cells mainly in the head region (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A); the npr-22prom::Venus expression was observed in head muscles, the I2 neurons, the MC neurons, the RIH neuron, the AIA neurons, the AUA neurons, the ASK neurons (strong in larval worms), the ASI neurons (strong in larval worms), a few B-type motorneurons in the posterior ventral nerve cord (variable), pharyngeal muscles, body wall muscles (weak), the intestine (weak), and a few classes of unidentified cells anterior to the nerve ring (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: Supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: Co-expression of established cell markers confirmed npr-22 expression in I2, MC, RIH, AIA, AUA, and posterior B-type motorneurons.
claims.source: In the I2, MC, RIH, AIA, AUA, and posterior B-type motorneurons, we confirmed the co-expression of established cell markers (Feng and Hope, 2013; Hao et al., 2001; Kim and Li, 2004; Macosko et al., 2009; Sze et al., 2002; Tomioka et al., 2006) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B–H).
claims.evidence: Supported by co-localization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B–H and citations to cell marker studies.

claims.claim: Multicopy expression of lury-1 decreased numbers of unlaid eggs in the uterus.
claims.source: This multicopy expression of lury-1 caused the following phenotypes. First, numbers of unlaid eggs in the uterus were decreased (Figure 4A,B).
claims.evidence: Supported by egg-in-worm assay data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claims.claim: The rate of egg-laying was not affected by multicopy lury-1 expression.
claims.source: The rate of egg-laying was not affected by the multicopy lury-1 expression (Figure 4C), indicating that in this strain the rate of ovulation is normal while egg-laying is constitutively facilitated and early-stage embryos are prematurely laid (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: Supported by egg-laying rate assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: In multicopy lury-1 strains, the rate of ovulation is normal while egg-laying is constitutively facilitated and early-stage embryos are prematurely laid.
claims.source: The rate of egg-laying was not affected by the multicopy lury-1 expression (Figure 4C), indicating that in this strain the rate of ovulation is normal while egg-laying is constitutively facilitated and early-stage embryos are prematurely laid (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: Inferred from combination of normal egg-laying rate and decreased eggs in uterus with early-stage embryos laid.

claims.claim: Multicopy lury-1 expression phenotypes meet the standard criteria to be classified as egg-laying constitutive (Egl-c).
claims.source: These phenotypes meet the standard criteria to be classified as egg-laying constitutive (Egl-c) (Hart, 2006) and are similar to those of the mutants previously described as Egl-c (Hawasli et al., 2004; Kwok et al., 2006; Ringstad and Horvitz, 2008) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B).
claims.evidence: Supported by comparison to established Egl-c criteria and similar mutants, with citations.

claims.claim: Multicopy expression of lury-1 reduced the rate of pharyngeal pumping.
claims.source: Second, the rate of pharyngeal pumping, which is a rhythmic muscle contraction required for food intake (Avery and You, 2012), was reduced (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: Supported by pharyngeal pumping assay data shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: Multicopy expression of lury-1 extended adult lifespan by 21–50%.
claims.source: Third, adult lifespan is extended as much as 21–50% (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 2, and Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by lifespan assay data shown in Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 2, and Supplementary file 1.

claims.claim: Ectopic expression of lury-1 in all neurons using the rimb-1 promoter caused similar phenotypes to multicopy lury-1 expression.
claims.source: The ectopic expression of lury-1 in all neurons using the rimb-1 promoter also caused the similar phenotypes (Figure 4B,D and Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by phenotypic data shown in Figure 4B,D and Supplementary file 1.

claims.claim: Multicopy expression of lury-1 attenuated roaming behavior.
claims.source: Fourth, roaming behavior, which was measured by the numbers of grid squares that were entered by the worm tracks (Fujiwara et al., 2002), was attenuated (Figure 4F).
claims.evidence: Supported by roaming assay data shown in Figure 4F and citation to method.

claims.claim: The Egl-c, slow-pumping, long-lived, and reduced-roaming phenotypes caused by multicopy lury-1 expression were all largely suppressed by deletion of npr-22.
claims.source: Importantly, these Egl-c, slow-pumping, long-lived, and reduced-roaming phenotypes were all largely suppressed by the deletion of npr-22 (Figure 4A,B,D,E,F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2, and Supplementary file 1), indicating that lury-1(+) functions upstream of npr-22.
claims.evidence: Supported by genetic suppression data shown in Figure 4A,B,D,E,F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2, and Supplementary file 1.

claims.claim: lury-1(+) functions upstream of npr-22.
claims.source: Importantly, these Egl-c, slow-pumping, long-lived, and reduced-roaming phenotypes were all largely suppressed by the deletion of npr-22 (Figure 4A,B,D,E,F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2, and Supplementary file 1), indicating that lury-1(+) functions upstream of npr-22.
claims.evidence: Inferred from genetic suppression experiments showing npr-22 deletion suppresses lury-1 overexpression phenotypes.

claims.claim: Injection of 10 µM LURY-1-1 or LURY-1-2 into wild-type worms reduced number of eggs retained in the uterus and pharyngeal pumping rate.
claims.source: When a 10 µM solution of either LURY-1-1 or LURY-1-2 was injected into wild-type worms, number of eggs retained in the uterus and pharyngeal pumping rate were reduced (Figure 5A,B), similar to worms carrying the lury-1(+) transgenic array (Figure 4B,D).
claims.evidence: Supported by peptide injection assay data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claims.claim: The effects of LURY-1 peptide injection were not observed in npr-22(ok1598) mutants.
claims.source: These effects of the injection of LURY-1 peptides were not observed in the npr-22(ok1598) mutants (Figure 5A,B).
claims.evidence: Supported by peptide injection assay data in npr-22 mutants shown in Figure 5A,B.

claims.claim: Administration of 10 µM FLP-7-3 did not cause Egl-c or slow-pumping phenotype.
claims.source: On the other hand, neither the administration of a 10 µM solution of another putative NPR-22 ligand, FLP-73, nor the multicopy expression of its precursor gene flp-7(+) caused any Egl-c or slow-pumping phenotype (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D).
claims.evidence: Supported by peptide injection and overexpression data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D.

claims.claim: Multicopy expression of flp-7(+) did not cause Egl-c or slow-pumping phenotype.
claims.source: On the other hand, neither the administration of a 10 µM solution of another putative NPR-22 ligand, FLP-73, nor the multicopy expression of its precursor gene flp-7(+) caused any Egl-c or slow-pumping phenotype (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D).
claims.evidence: Supported by overexpression data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D.

claims.claim: The fluorescence of lury-1prom::lury-1::Venus reporter in coelomocytes was decreased in starved worms and rapidly restored by subsequent refeeding.
claims.source: When Venus is C-terminally fused to the LURY-1 coding region, the fluorescence of the Venus reporter in coelomocytes was decreased in starved worms, and was rapidly restored by subsequent refeeding (Figure 6A,B).
claims.evidence: Supported by coelomocyte uptake assay data shown in Figure 6A,B.

claims.claim: The fluorescence of signal sequence-tagged GFP expressed in body wall muscles and accumulated in coelomocytes was unchanged by starvation or refeeding.
claims.source: When GFP is fused with a signal sequence for secretion and expressed in body wall muscles, the fluorescence is also accumulated in coelomocytes (Fares and Greenwald, 2001) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A). This fluorescence reporting the constitutive secretion from muscles was unchanged by starvation or subsequent refeeding (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: Supported by control experiment data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B and citation.

claims.claim: Venus alone expressed under the lury-1 promoter showed fluorescence in M1 and M2 that was unaffected by the presence or absence of food.
claims.source: Moreover, when Venus alone was expressed under the lury-1 promoter, the fluorescence in M1 and M2 was unaffected by the presence or absence of food (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: Supported by control experiment data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: The secretion of LURY-1 peptides is positively controlled by the presence of food.
claims.source: Collectively, these results suggest that the secretion of LURY-1 peptides is positively controlled by the presence of food.
claims.evidence: Inferred from coelomocyte uptake assays showing food-dependent changes in LURY-1::Venus secretion but not in control reporters.

claims.claim: Deletion of lury-1 or npr-22 by itself did not cause egg-laying defective, fast-pumping, short-lived, or increased-roaming phenotype under normal conditions, except for a weak egg-laying defective phenotype in lury-1(gk961835) mutants.
claims.source: The deletion of lury-1 or npr-22 (Figure 2A) by itself did not cause egg-laying defective, fast-pumping, short-lived, or increased-roaming phenotype under normal conditions (Figure 4B,D,E,F and Supplementary file 1), except for a weak egg-laying defective phenotype shown by the lury-1(gk961835) mutants (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: Supported by phenotypic analysis data shown in Figure 4B,D,E,F and Supplementary file 1.

claims.claim: The lury-1(gk961835) and npr-22(ok1598) mutants normally retained eggs in their body after 2 hr starvation.
claims.source: We found that the lury-1(gk961835) and npr-22(ok1598) mutants normally retained eggs in their body after 2 hr starvation (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: Supported by starvation/refeeding assay data shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: In lury-1(gk961835) and npr-22(ok1598) mutants, the numbers of eggs laid during the initial 30 min refeeding period were decreased.
claims.source: However, in the lury-1(gk961835) and npr-22(ok1598) mutants, the numbers of eggs laid during the initial 30 min refeeding period were decreased (Figure 6D), and the numbers of unlaid eggs in the uterus returned to baseline of fed worms more slowly during the refeeding period than in wild type (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: Supported by refeeding assay data shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: In lury-1(gk961835) and npr-22(ok1598) mutants, the numbers of unlaid eggs in the uterus returned to baseline more slowly during refeeding than in wild type.
claims.source: However, in the lury-1(gk961835) and npr-22(ok1598) mutants, the numbers of eggs laid during the initial 30 min refeeding period were decreased (Figure 6D), and the numbers of unlaid eggs in the uterus returned to baseline of fed worms more slowly during the refeeding period than in wild type (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: Supported by refeeding assay data shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: The lury-1(gk961835) and npr-22(ok1598) mutants normally elevated their pharyngeal pumping shortly after refeeding, but showed satiety-induced suppression of pharyngeal pumping more slowly than wild type.
claims.source: We also found that the lury-1(gk961835) and npr-22(ok1598) mutants normally elevated their pharyngeal pumping shortly after refeeding, but showed their satiety-induced suppression of pharyngeal pumping (You et al., 2008) more slowly than wild type (Figure 6E).
claims.evidence: Supported by refeeding pumping assay data shown in Figure 6E and citation to You et al., 2008.

claims.claim: The activities of LURY-1 peptides and NPR-22 are latent under normal culture conditions and exert their actions under conditions that induce hyperactivation of pharynx.
claims.source: These results might suggest that the activities of LURY-1 peptides and NPR-22 are latent under normal culture conditions and that LURY-1 peptides exert their actions under certain conditions that induce hyperactivation of pharynx, such as abrupt refeeding after starvation, along with other signals such as insulin and TGF-β (You et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: Inferred from observations that mutants show normal baseline phenotypes but altered responses during refeeding, with citation to You et al., 2008.

claims.claim: Both npr-22a and npr-22b isoforms can restore the egg-laying-stimulatory and feeding-suppressive effects of multicopy lury-1(+) expression in the npr-22 mutant background.
claims.source: When either of the two npr-22 isoforms (npr-22a and npr-22b; Figure 2A) was expressed under the authentic npr-22 promoter, both isoforms were found to be able to restore the egg-laying-stimulatory and feeding-suppressive effects of the multicopy expression of lury-1(+) in the npr-22 mutant background (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A), consistent with the results of the [Ca2+]i assays showing that both isoforms are functional LURY-1 peptides receptors (Figure 2E,F).
claims.evidence: Supported by rescue experiment data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A, and calcium assay data.

claims.claim: Expression of npr-22a driven by the ceh-19 promoter was sufficient for mediating the suppressive effects of lury-1(+) on feeding.
claims.source: We found that the expression of npr-22a driven by the ceh-19 promoter, which induces the expression in MC, ADF, and PHA (Feng and Hope, 2013) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C), was sufficient for the mediation of the suppressive effects of lury-1(+) on feeding (Figure 7A).
claims.evidence: Supported by cell-specific rescue data shown in Figure 7A and citation to Feng and Hope, 2013.

claims.claim: Expression of npr-22a in npr-22-expressing cells other than MC did not affect feeding in the peIs2413[lury-1(+)]; npr-22 background.
claims.source: In contrast, when npr-22a was expressed in npr-22-expressing cells other than MC (driven by the ins-1, ges-1, cat-1, flp-15, myo-2, myo-3, and acr-2 promoters), in ADF (driven by the cat-1 promoter), or in PHA (driven by the flp-15 promoter), feeding was not affected in the peIs2413[lury-1(+)]; npr-22 background (Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that the expression of npr-22a in MC is important.
claims.evidence: Supported by cell-specific rescue data shown in Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: MC-specific expression of npr-22a using the FLP-FRT gene activation system was sufficient for mediating the suppressive effects of lury-1(+) on feeding in the npr-22 mutant background.
claims.source: The MC-specific expression of npr-22a using this system was sufficient for the mediation of the suppressive effects of lury-1(+) on feeding in the npr-22 mutant background (Figure 7D).
claims.evidence: Supported by MC-specific rescue data shown in Figure 7D.

claims.claim: NPR-22 is likely to act in MC neurons to control feeding.
claims.source: Therefore, we conclude that NPR-22 is likely to act in MC, which are known to be important neurons for the stimulation of food pumping (Raizen et al., 1995; Trojanowski et al., 2014), to control feeding.
claims.evidence: Inferred from cell-specific rescue experiments showing MC expression is sufficient and necessary, with citations to MC function studies.

claims.claim: Expression of npr-22a driven by the ceh-19 promoter rescued the shortened lifespan of peIs2413[lury-1(+)]; npr-22.
claims.source: The expression of npr-22a driven by the ceh-19 promoter also rescued the shortened lifespan of peIs2413[lury-1(+)]; npr-22 (Figure 7E), implying the relationship between feeding suppression and extended lifespan mediated by lury-1(+).
claims.evidence: Supported by lifespan rescue data shown in Figure 7E.

claims.claim: There is a relationship between feeding suppression and extended lifespan mediated by lury-1(+).
claims.source: The expression of npr-22a driven by the ceh-19 promoter also rescued the shortened lifespan of peIs2413[lury-1(+)]; npr-22 (Figure 7E), implying the relationship between feeding suppression and extended lifespan mediated by lury-1(+).
claims.evidence: Inferred from observation that the same cell-specific rescue (ceh-19 promoter) restores both feeding and lifespan phenotypes.

claims.claim: Expression of npr-22a in serotonergic/dopaminergic neurons under the cat-1 promoter restored the Egl-c phenotype in peIs2413[lury-1(+)]; npr-22 strain.
claims.source: In the regulation of egg-laying, the Egl-c phenotype reappeared when npr-22a was expressed in serotonergic/dopaminergic neurons under the cat-1 promoter in the peIs2413[lury-1(+)]; npr-22 strain (Figure 8A).
claims.evidence: Supported by cell-specific rescue data shown in Figure 8A.

claims.claim: The RIH neuron is the only cell in which the expression patterns induced by the npr-22 and cat-1 promoters overlap.
claims.source: The RIH neuron is the only cell in which the expression patterns induced by the npr-22 and cat-1 promoters overlap (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
claims.evidence: Supported by co-localization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claims.claim: The Egl-c phenotype was restored by expression of npr-22a under the slt-1 promoter.
claims.source: Moreover, the Egl-c phenotype was also restored by the expression of npr-22a under the slt-1 promoter (Figure 8A), which is also active in the RIH neuron (Hao et al., 2001) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E).
claims.evidence: Supported by cell-specific rescue data shown in Figure 8A and citation to Hao et al., 2001.

claims.claim: RIH-specific expression of npr-22a driven by the FLP-FRT gene activation system rescued the npr-22 mutant phenotype in egg-laying regulation.
claims.source: We also observed that the RIH-specific expression of npr-22a driven by the FLP-FRT gene activation system using npr-22prom and cat-1prom (Figures 7B and 8B) rescued the npr-22 mutant phenotype in the egg-laying regulation (Figure 8C), whereas the expression of npr-22a in npr-22-expressing cells other than RIH had no effects (Figure 8A,C and Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: Supported by RIH-specific rescue data shown in Figure 8C.

claims.claim: The action of NPR-22 in RIH is important for the facilitation of egg-laying.
claims.source: These results suggest that the action of NPR-22 in RIH is important for the facilitation of egg-laying.
claims.evidence: Inferred from cell-specific rescue experiments showing RIH expression is sufficient and necessary for egg-laying regulation.

claims.claim: The RIH neuron does not express serotonin biosynthesis enzymes but uptakes serotonin from extracellular space through MOD-5/SERT.
claims.source: The RIH neuron does not express serotonin [5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT)] biosynthesis enzymes but uptake serotonin from extracellular space through MOD-5/serotonin reuptake transporter (SERT) (Jafari et al., 2011), and serotonin regulates many food-associated processes including egg-laying (Chase and Koelle, 2007; Sze et al., 2000).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Jafari et al., 2011, Chase and Koelle, 2007, and Sze et al., 2000.

claims.claim: Serotonin regulates many food-associated processes including egg-laying.
claims.source: The RIH neuron does not express serotonin [5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT)] biosynthesis enzymes but uptake serotonin from extracellular space through MOD-5/serotonin reuptake transporter (SERT) (Jafari et al., 2011), and serotonin regulates many food-associated processes including egg-laying (Chase and Koelle, 2007; Sze et al., 2000).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Chase and Koelle, 2007 and Sze et al., 2000.

claims.claim: The Egl-c phenotype caused by multicopy lury-1(+) expression was partially suppressed by a nonsense mutation in cat-1.
claims.source: The Egl-c phenotype caused by the multicopy expression of lury-1(+) was partially suppressed by a nonsense mutation in cat-1 (Figure 9A), which encodes the putative synaptic vesicular transporter for serotonin, dopamine, tyramine, and octopamine (Chase and Koelle, 2007; Duerr et al., 1999).
claims.evidence: Supported by genetic interaction data shown in Figure 9A and citations to Chase and Koelle, 2007 and Duerr et al., 1999.

claims.claim: A null mutation in tph-1 suppressed the Egl-c phenotype caused by multicopy lury-1(+) expression.
claims.source: Moreover, a null mutation in tph-1, which encodes the serotonin synthetic enzyme tryptophan hydroxylase, suppressed the Egl-c phenotype (Figure 9A), whereas a null mutation in cat-2, which encodes the dopamine synthetic enzyme tyrosine hydroxylase, did not affect egg-laying (Figure 9A).
claims.evidence: Supported by genetic interaction data shown in Figure 9A.

claims.claim: A null mutation in cat-2 did not affect egg-laying in the context of multicopy lury-1(+) expression.
claims.source: Moreover, a null mutation in tph-1, which encodes the serotonin synthetic enzyme tryptophan hydroxylase, suppressed the Egl-c phenotype (Figure 9A), whereas a null mutation in cat-2, which encodes the dopamine synthetic enzyme tyrosine hydroxylase, did not affect egg-laying (Figure 9A).
claims.evidence: Supported by genetic interaction data shown in Figure 9A.

claims.claim: When mod-5(n3314) and mod-5(n822) mutants experienced starvation and refeeding, the numbers of unlaid eggs decreased more slowly than wild type during the refeeding period.
claims.source: When two alleles of mod-5 mutants, mod-5(n3314) and mod-5(n822), experienced starvation and then refed, the numbers of unlaid eggs decreased more slowly than wild type during the refeeding period (Figure 9B), like in the lury-1 and npr-22 mutants (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: Supported by refeeding assay data shown in Figure 9B.

claims.claim: The Egl-c phenotype caused by multicopy lury-1(+) expression was partially suppressed by mutations in mod-5.
claims.source: Furthermore, the Egl-c phenotype caused by the multicopy lury-1(+) expression was partially suppressed by the mutations in mod-5 (Figure 9C).
claims.evidence: Supported by genetic interaction data shown in Figure 9C.

claims.claim: LURY-1 peptides facilitate egg-laying through serotonin signaling derived from RIH.
claims.source: Collectively, these results imply that LURY-1 peptides facilitate egg-laying through serotonin signaling derived from RIH.
claims.evidence: Inferred from genetic interactions with serotonin pathway genes and cell-specific rescue experiments.

claims.claim: LURY-1 peptides convey information about food-evoked activation of pharynx to control multiple processes through the broadly expressed NPR-22.
claims.source: Based on these results, together with the observation that the lury-1(gk961835) and npr-22(ok1598) deletion mutants reduced egg-laying and elevated feeding during the refeeding period after starvation, we propose a model in which LURY-1 peptides convey information about the food-evoked activation of pharynx to control multiple processes through the broadly expressed NPR-22 (Figure 9D).
claims.evidence: Proposed model based on integration of expression patterns, secretion data, mutant phenotypes, and cell-specific rescue experiments.

claims.claim: The distance and lack of synaptic connection between LURY-1 peptides-secreting neurons and RIH suggest that LURY-1 peptides can function in a hormone-like manner.
claims.source: The distance and the lack of synaptic connection between the LURY-1 peptides-secreting neurons and RIH suggest that LURY-1 peptides can function in a hormone-like manner.
claims.evidence: Inferred from anatomical considerations and the observation that LURY-1::Venus is found in coelomocytes.

claims.claim: FLP-7-3 elicited a much weaker calcium response in CHO-NPR-22 cells than LURY-1 peptides.
claims.source: However, in our hands, FLP-7–3 elicited a much weaker calcium response in CHO-NPR-22 cells than LURY-1 peptides (Figure 2E,F) and did not affect egg laying nor pharyngeal pumping (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), both of which are shown to be regulated by NPR-22 (Figure 4).
claims.evidence: Supported by calcium assay comparison data shown in Figure 2E,F.

claims.claim: FLP-7-3 did not affect egg laying nor pharyngeal pumping.
claims.source: However, in our hands, FLP-7–3 elicited a much weaker calcium response in CHO-NPR-22 cells than LURY-1 peptides (Figure 2E,F) and did not affect egg laying nor pharyngeal pumping (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), both of which are shown to be regulated by NPR-22 (Figure 4).
claims.evidence: Supported by functional assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The lury-1(gk961835) and npr-22(ok1598) deletion mutants showed similar egg-laying and feeding phenotypes.
claims.source: Together with the finding that the lury-1(gk961835) and npr-22(ok1598) deletion mutants showed similar egg-laying and feeding phenotypes (Figure 6C–E), we conclude that LURY-1 peptides act as endogenous ligands of NPR-22.
claims.evidence: Supported by mutant phenotype comparison data shown in Figure 6C–E.

claims.claim: The two classes of NPR-22 ligands, LURY-1 peptides and FLP-7-derived peptides, mediate at least in part distinct functions.
claims.source: The findings in our study and a previous study (Palamiuc et al., 2017) suggest that the two classes of NPR-22 ligands, LURY-1 peptides and FLP-7-derived peptides, mediate, at least in part, distinct functions.
claims.evidence: Inferred from differences in potency and functional effects between LURY-1 peptides and FLP-7-3, with citation to Palamiuc et al., 2017.

claims.claim: Suppression of feeding, facilitation of egg-laying, and attenuation of locomotory behavior are all induced by the presence of abundant food.
claims.source: Intriguingly, all the phenotypes caused by the multicopy expression of lury-1(+) (Figure 4) are strongly related to feeding. Suppression of feeding, facilitation of egg-laying, and attenuation of locomotory behavior are all induced by the presence of abundant food (Waggoner et al., 2000; You et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Waggoner et al., 2000 and You et al., 2008.

claims.claim: Lifespan extension has been closely associated with feeding.
claims.source: Lifespan extension has also been closely associated with feeding (Lakowski and Hekimi, 1998).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Lakowski and Hekimi, 1998.

claims.claim: The lury-1(+)-mediated lifespan extension was caused by reduced feeding.
claims.source: Our results that both the lifespan and feeding phenotypes of the npr-22 mutants were rescued by the npr-22 expression under the ceh-19 promoter (Figure 7A,E) imply that the lury-1(+)-mediated lifespan extension was caused by reduced feeding.
claims.evidence: Inferred from observation that the same cell-specific rescue restores both feeding and lifespan phenotypes.

claims.claim: LURY-1 peptides transmit food-related signals from pharynx, which plays critical roles in the C. elegans digestive system.
claims.source: Taken together, these observations raise the possibility that LURY-1 peptides transmit food-related signals from pharynx, which plays critical roles in the C. elegans digestive system (Albertson and Thomson, 1976).
claims.evidence: Inferred from expression in pharyngeal neurons, food-dependent secretion, and food-related phenotypes, with citation to Albertson and Thomson, 1976.

claims.claim: The mode of action of LURY-1 peptides is reminiscent of mammalian PYY and PP, which are anorexigenic peptides derived from digestive organs.
claims.source: Such a hypothesis is reminiscent of the mode of action of mammalian PYY and PP, which are also anorexigenic peptides derived from digestive organs (Loh et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: Comparison to mammalian peptides based on similar functional properties, with citation to Loh et al., 2015.

claims.claim: Feeding suppressive effects of RYamide-containing peptides have been observed in blowflies and kuruma shrimps.
claims.source: Interestingly, feeding suppressive effects of RYamide-containing peptides have also been observed in blowflies (Maeda et al., 2015) and kuruma shrimps (Mekata et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Maeda et al., 2015 and Mekata et al., 2017.

claims.source: Although serotonin signaling in RIH is highly likely to mediate the effects of LURY-1 peptides on egg laying, the fact that serotonin signaling functions in HSN to facilitate egg-laying (Chase and Koelle, 2007) may complicate the interpretation of our results.

The M1 neuron responds to short wavelength light and stimulates spitting behavior (Bhatla et al., 2015), whereas the M2 neurons possess gap junction with the MC neurons and are stimulatory for pharyngeal pumping (Albertson and Thomson, 1976; Trojanowski et al., 2014).

results.result: LURY-1-1 and LURY-1-2 are novel C. elegans neuropeptides derived from a luqin/RYamide orthologous precursor that function as endogenous ligands for NPR-22. The peptides were biochemically purified and structurally characterized, showing C-terminal RYamide motifs and activating both NPR-22 isoforms with nanomolar potency, significantly more potently than the previously reported ligand FLP-7-3.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C35-C52 provide comprehensive biochemical, structural, and functional evidence. The purification strategy using CHO-CG5811 cells (C35-C38), mass spectrometry confirmation (C39-C40), synthetic peptide validation (C41), sequence analysis showing luqin characteristics (C2, C42), and dose-response calcium assays demonstrating receptor activation (C44-C52) collectively establish LURY-1 peptides as bona fide NPR-22 ligands. The comparison with FLP-7-3 (C50) strengthens the claim of physiological relevance.

results.result: LURY-1 peptides are specifically expressed in and secreted from M1 and M2 pharyngeal neurons. Expression is constitutive in M1 across all developmental stages, while M2 expression increases from the L4 stage onward. The translational reporter demonstrates secretion into the body cavity via coelomocyte uptake.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C53-C57 are well-supported by fluorescence microscopy data showing cell-specific expression patterns (C53-C55), co-localization with established markers, and coelomocyte uptake of the translational reporter (C56-C57). The developmental expression pattern is quantified across multiple stages (C54-C55). These data convincingly demonstrate the cellular source and secretory nature of LURY-1 peptides.

results.result: NPR-22 is broadly expressed in multiple cell types in the head region, including neurons (I2, MC, RIH, AIA, AUA, ASK, ASI, B-type motorneurons), muscles (head, pharyngeal, body wall), and intestine. Expression was confirmed by co-localization with established cell markers.
results.evaluation: Claims C58-C59 are supported by comprehensive fluorescence microscopy data showing npr-22 promoter-driven reporter expression across multiple tissues and confirmation via co-expression with established cell markers. The broad expression pattern is well-documented and provides the anatomical basis for understanding LURY-1 peptide signaling targets.

results.result: Multicopy expression of lury-1 causes multiple food-related phenotypes including egg-laying constitutive (Egl-c), reduced pharyngeal pumping, extended lifespan (21-50%), and attenuated roaming behavior. All phenotypes are suppressed by npr-22 deletion, establishing that lury-1 functions upstream of npr-22.
results.evaluation: Claims C60-C69 provide strong genetic evidence through gain-of-function experiments. The multicopy lury-1 phenotypes (C60-C67) are well-characterized across multiple behavioral and physiological parameters with appropriate statistical analysis. The genetic epistasis demonstrated by npr-22 deletion suppressing all lury-1 overexpression phenotypes (C68) convincingly establishes the pathway relationship (C69). The use of multiple independent transgenic lines strengthens the conclusions.

results.result: Direct injection of synthetic LURY-1 peptides (10 µM) into wild-type worms recapitulates the multicopy lury-1 phenotypes (reduced eggs in uterus and pharyngeal pumping), and these effects require NPR-22. In contrast, FLP-7-3 peptide injection or flp-7 overexpression produces no phenotype.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C73 provide critical validation that the peptides themselves, not other effects of genetic manipulation, cause the observed phenotypes. The peptide injection experiments (C70-C71) demonstrate sufficiency and NPR-22-dependence. The negative results with FLP-7-3 (C72-C73) support the specificity of LURY-1 peptides as physiologically relevant NPR-22 ligands, though the injection concentration and delivery method could be further optimized.

results.result: LURY-1 peptide secretion is positively regulated by food availability. The fluorescence of lury-1::Venus reporter in coelomocytes decreases during starvation and rapidly recovers upon refeeding, while control reporters (constitutively secreted ssGFP and cytoplasmic Venus) are unaffected by food status.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C77 are supported by well-controlled coelomocyte uptake assays. The food-dependent changes in LURY-1::Venus secretion (C74) are validated by appropriate controls showing no changes in constitutive secretion (C75) or promoter activity (C76). The inference that secretion is food-regulated (C77) is reasonable, though the mechanism of regulation remains unclear and could involve transcriptional, post-translational, or vesicle release control.

results.result: Loss-of-function mutations in lury-1 or npr-22 show minimal phenotypes under normal conditions but exhibit delayed responses during refeeding after starvation, including slower egg-laying resumption and prolonged pharyngeal pumping. This suggests LURY-1/NPR-22 signaling is specifically activated during hyperactive pharyngeal states.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C83 provide important loss-of-function data complementing the gain-of-function studies. The starvation-refeeding paradigm (C79-C82) reveals context-dependent functions that explain why baseline phenotypes are minimal (C78). The interpretation that LURY-1/NPR-22 activity is latent under normal conditions and activated during pharyngeal hyperactivation (C83) is reasonable, though the molecular mechanisms underlying this conditional activation remain to be determined.

results.result: NPR-22 acts in MC neurons to mediate LURY-1-dependent feeding suppression and lifespan extension. Cell-specific rescue experiments using multiple promoters and the FLP-FRT system demonstrate that MC-specific npr-22 expression is both necessary and sufficient for these phenotypes.
results.evaluation: Claims C84-C90 provide rigorous cell-specific rescue data. The use of multiple promoters (C85-C86) and the FLP-FRT system for single-cell specificity (C87) convincingly localizes NPR-22 function to MC neurons for feeding control (C88). The parallel rescue of lifespan and feeding phenotypes by the same cell-specific expression (C89) supports a mechanistic link between feeding suppression and longevity (C90), though causality requires further validation.

results.result: NPR-22 acts in the RIH neuron to mediate LURY-1-dependent egg-laying facilitation. Multiple promoters (cat-1, slt-1) that overlap only in RIH restore the Egl-c phenotype, and FLP-FRT-mediated RIH-specific expression is sufficient for rescue.
results.evaluation: Claims C91-C95 use similar rigorous cell-specific approaches as for MC neurons. The identification of RIH as the unique overlapping cell between cat-1 and npr-22 expression (C92), confirmation with slt-1 promoter (C93), and FLP-FRT validation (C94) provide strong evidence that NPR-22 acts in RIH for egg-laying regulation (C95). The anatomical separation of feeding and egg-laying control to different neurons is well-established.

results.result: LURY-1 peptides facilitate egg-laying through serotonin signaling downstream of NPR-22 in RIH. Genetic interactions show that mutations in serotonin pathway genes (tph-1, cat-1, mod-5) suppress the lury-1 overexpression Egl-c phenotype, and mod-5 mutants phenocopy lury-1/npr-22 mutants in refeeding assays.
results.evaluation: Claims C96-C103 establish a signaling pathway from LURY-1/NPR-22 to serotonin. The genetic interactions (C98-C102) show specificity for serotonin (tph-1, mod-5) over dopamine (cat-2), and the mod-5 mutant phenotypes (C101) support the model. However, the partial suppression by serotonin pathway mutations (C98, C102) suggests additional parallel pathways may exist. The inference that RIH-derived serotonin mediates the effects (C103) is reasonable given C96-C97, though direct measurement of serotonin release would strengthen this conclusion.

results.result: LURY-1 peptides function as a negative feedback signal for satiety regulation, transmitting information about food-evoked pharyngeal activation to broadly expressed NPR-22 receptors in a hormone-like manner to coordinate multiple food-related processes.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C104-C105 synthesize the experimental findings into a coherent model. The negative feedback interpretation (C6) is supported by food-dependent secretion (C74-C77), feeding suppression upon overexpression (C64), and delayed satiety in mutants (C82-C83). The hormone-like function (C105) is supported by coelomocyte uptake (C56-C57) and lack of synaptic connections between M1/M2 and target neurons. The model (C104) integrates expression, secretion, and functional data, though some mechanistic details remain to be elucidated.

results.result: LURY-1 peptides, not FLP-7-derived peptides, are the physiologically relevant endogenous ligands for NPR-22 in feeding and egg-laying regulation. FLP-7-3 shows much weaker receptor activation and no functional effects, while lury-1 and npr-22 mutants show similar phenotypes.
results.evaluation: Claims C106-C109 address the discrepancy with prior literature identifying FLP-7 as an NPR-22 ligand. The comparative data showing weaker FLP-7-3 potency (C106), lack of functional effects (C107), and similar lury-1/npr-22 mutant phenotypes (C108) support LURY-1 as the primary physiological ligand. The conclusion that the two ligand classes mediate distinct functions (C109) is reasonable, though the specific roles of FLP-7 peptides remain unclear and warrant further investigation.

results.result: The LURY-1/NPR-22 system represents a conserved mechanism for feeding regulation analogous to mammalian anorexigenic peptides from digestive organs. The mode of action resembles mammalian PYY/PP, and feeding-suppressive effects of RYamide peptides are observed across invertebrate species.
results.evaluation: Claims C110-C115 make evolutionary and comparative arguments. While the functional parallels to mammalian systems (C110-C112, C114) and conservation across invertebrates (C115) are supported by citations, the direct evolutionary relationship remains speculative. The pharynx as analogous to mammalian digestive organs (C113) is reasonable but the anatomical and functional differences are substantial. These comparative claims provide valuable context but require more direct comparative studies to be fully supported.

results.result: Background claims establishing the context for feeding regulation in mammals and C. elegans, the NPY/RYamide peptide family characteristics, and prior work on related receptors and peptides. These include established knowledge about mammalian satiety hormones, C. elegans feeding behavior, luqin/RYamide peptide evolution, and previous identification of CG5811 and NPR-22.
results.evaluation: Claims C7-C34, C116-C119 are primarily literature-based background claims supported by appropriate citations to established work. These provide essential context for interpreting the novel findings but do not represent new experimental results from this study. The citations appear appropriate and the background knowledge is accurately represented.
